ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
To promote her school's annual Kite Olympics, Genevieve makes a small kite and a large kite for a bulletin board display. The kites look like the one in the diagram. For her small kite Genevieve draws the kite on a one-inch grid. For the large kite she triples both the height and width of the entire grid.
<image1>


What is the number of square inches in the area of the small kite?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a kite-shaped quadrilateral drawn on a dot-grid. The vertices of the kite all lie on grid points; the left and right vertices are on the same horizontal grid line, the top vertex is located in the middle position above them, and the bottom vertex is located in the middle position below them. Counting the grid intervals, it can be seen: the horizontal diagonal from the left vertex to the right vertex has length 6 grid units; the vertical diagonal from the top vertex to the bottom vertex has length 7 grid units. Reasoning: The small kite is drawn on a one-inch grid, so these two diagonals are respectively 6 inches and 7 inches. The area of a kite equals half the product of the two mutually perpendicular diagonals, so the area is 1/2 × 6 × 7 = 21 square inches.
